discovery: First images of the shadows of supermassive black holes (M87* and Sgr A*) with the Event Horizon Telescope

nominees.name: Sheperd S. Doeleman
nominees.affiliation: Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian, USA

nominees.name: J. Anton Zensus
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute for Radio Astronomy, Bonn, Germany

subfield: Astrophysics / black hole physics / very-long-baseline interferometry
motivation: Stellar orbits established that a four-million-solar-mass compact object sits at the centre of our Galaxy, but they probe gravity at hundreds of Schwarzschild radii. The Event Horizon Telescope reached the horizon itself. Falcke predicted in 2000 that a black hole shadow would be visible at millimetre wavelengths. Doeleman built the first event-horizon-scale detections of Sgr A* and led the growth of a planet-wide 1.3 mm VLBI array. Zensus drove the European effort and the collaboration's organisation. Together they produced the images of M87* (2019) and Sgr A* (2022), plus polarimetric and multi-year follow-up. The ring sizes match general-relativistic predictions for masses measured independently, including our stellar-orbit mass for Sgr A*. This is a triumph of new technology, patient repeated measurement and rigorous independent cross-checking. It moved black hole horizons from inference to direct observation and opened a new observational frontier for testing gravity.
